column2: Panyajiva and "apanika" are shopkeepers; "nyasa" and "upanidhi" are deposits (masculine); "vipana" is sale; then numbers: "sankhya", and numerals up to "ashtadasha" (eighteen) are used with counted things in three genders.

Vimshati (twenty) and the like are always singular; all of them are used both of the counted and the number; in the sense of number they take dual and plural; and those up to "navati" (ninety) are feminine.
Pankti (ten), then "shata", "sahasra" and so on, each ten times the one before; measures: by finger, "prastha"; five "gunja" seeds make a "masha"...
...sixteen of them make an "aksha"/"karsha" (masculine or neuter); four karshas make a "pala"; "suvarna" and "vista" are measures of gold, "aksha" of gold; "kuruvista" is a pala.
Tula (feminine) is a hundred palas; "bhara" is twenty tulas; "karshapana" is a coin of a karsha; "pana" of a copper karsha.
Wealth: "dravya, vitta, svapateya, riktha, riktha, dhana, vasu"; "riti" (brass, feminine), "arakuta" (masculine); then "tamraka" (copper).
Shulba, "audumbara" (copper); iron: "tikshna, kalayasa, ayasa"; "kshara" (alkali), "kacha" (glass); "chapala", "rasa", "suta" (mercury) in quicksilver.
Garala (poison), "mahisha" (buffalo horn); tin and lead: "trapu", "sisaka"; "hindira" and "abdhikapha" are cuttlefish bone and foam; "madhuchchhishta" and "siktha" are beeswax.
Ranga and "vanga" (tin); "picu", "sthula", "kulati"; "manahshila" (realgar); "yavakshara" (saltpetre-like alkali), "pakya"; "tvakkshira", "vamshalochana" (bamboo manna).
Vrishala, "jaghanyaja", "shudra", "chandala" and the mixed castes are the lowest; "karu" and "shilpi" are craftsmen; their guild is "shreni", among those of the same trade.
Rangajiva (dyer), "chitrakara" (painter), "tvashta", "takshan", "vardhaki" (carpenter), "nadindhama" (glass-blower), "svarnakara" (goldsmith), "napita" (barber), "antavasayin".
Javala lives by goats; "devala" by serving gods; "shailusha" is an actor living on his wife; "bhritaka" and "bhritibhuk" are hired servants.
Vivarna, "pamara", "nicha", "prakrita", "prithagjana" (low, common people); "vihina", "upasada", "jalma"; servants: "bhritya", "dasa", "cheta".
Patu, "peshala", "daksha" are skilful; "mrigayu" and "lubdhaka" a hunter; "chandala" is "divakirti"; "pusta" is plaster-work and similar crafts.

Panchalika and "putrika" are a doll; "varkara" is a young animal; "manjusha", "petaka", "peda" are baskets and chests, alike; "pratima", "pratikriti" an image; "varga" are groups, beginning with Brahma.
One who goes together is "sadhryan"; one who goes crosswise is "tiryan"; "vachoyukti"; "patu" and "vagmi" are eloquent; "vavaduka" is a talker.
Jalpaka, "vachala", "vachata" are talkative, of much blameworthy speech; "apadhvasta" and "dhikkrita" are despised; "baddha", "kilita", "samyata" are bound.
Varana, "shabdana", "nandivadin", "nanvikara" are alike; "vyasanarta" and "uparakta" are two (afflicted); "baddha", "kilita", "samyata" are bound.
Vihista and "vyakula" are alike (distressed); "nrishamsa", "krura", "ghataka" are cruel and murderous; "papa", "dhurta", "vanchaka" the sinful, wily, deceitful; "vaideha" and "balisha" are fools.
Kadarya, "kripana", "kshudra" are miserly; "margana", "yachaka", "arthin" are beggars; "ahankaravan" and "ahamyu" are proud; "shubhamyu" is possessed of auspiciousness.
Kanta, "manorama", "ruchya", "hridya" are pleasing; "ishta" and "abhipsita" desired; "asara", "phalgu", "shunya" are worthless; "mukhya", "varya", "vareṇya" are chief.
Shreyas, "shreshtha", "pushkala" are best; "pragrya", "agrya", "agriya", "agrima" are foremost; "uru" and "vipula" are broad; "pina" and "pivan" are stout; "sthula", "pivara" are fat.
Stoka, "alpa", "kshullaka" are small; "sukshma", "shlakshna", "dabhra", "krisha", "tanu" are slight and slender; "matra", "kutila", "vakra" curved; "bhuyishtha", "puruha", "puru" are abundant.
Akhanda, "purna", "sakala" are whole; "upakantha", "antika", "abhitas" are near; "samipa", "sannidha", "abhyasa" are nearness; "nedishtha" and "susamipaka" are very near.
Davishtha is very far; "vritta", "nistala", "vartula" are round; "uchcha", "pramshu", "unnata", "udagra" are high; "dhruva", "nitya", "sanatana" are eternal.
Aviddha, "kutila", "bhugna", "vellita", "vakra" are crooked; "chanchala" and "tarala" are unsteady; "kathora", "jathara", "dridha" are hard and firm.
Pratyagra, "abhinava", "navya", "navina", "nutana", "nava" are new; "ekatana" is one-pointed; "ananyavritti"; "uchchanda" is fierce; "avilambita" is unhesitating.
Uchchavacha and "naikabheda" are of many kinds; "sambadha" and "kalila" are crowded; "timita" and "stimita" are wet or still; "abhiyoga" and "abhigraha" are attack.
Sphati is increase; "pratha" is fame; "samahara" and "samuchchaya" are collection; "apahara" and "apachaya" diminution; "vihara" is roaming about.
Pratyahara (withdrawal), "upadana" (taking up), "nirhara" (removal), "abhyavakarshana" (drawing out); "vighna", "antaraya", "pratyuha" (obstacle); "asana" and "sthiti" (sitting, state).
Sannidhi and "sannikarsha" are proximity; "sankrama" is passage over a difficult place; "upalambha" and "anubhava" are experience; "pratyadesha" and "nirakriti" are rejection.
Parirambha, "parishvanga", "samshlesha", "upaguhana" are embrace; "anuma" (inference) from "paksha", "hetu" and the like; "dimba" and "bhramara" (confusion) and "viplava" (disorder).
Knowledge of an object not in contact, obtained from words, is called verbal testimony; knowledge of likeness from seeing similarity is "upamana" (comparison).

Arthapatti (presumption) is knowledge of another matter without which the seen effect would not be; "abhava" (non-perception) is the knowledge "it is not on earth" when the counterpart is not apprehended. Hari has thus spoken the names and genders for the understanding of men.
They go to the Maharloka, and from Maharloka to Janaloka, when Hari, in Rudra's form, has burned the world by the breath of his mouth.
Then clouds of many forms, with lightning, arise and, raining for a hundred years, quench the fire that has risen.
When the waters stand covering the region of the Seven Sages, the wind for a hundred years, from the breath of Vishnu's mouth, destroys those clouds.
Having drunk the wind, the Lord Hari sleeps on Shesha in the single ocean, bearing the form of Brahma, praised by the Siddhas dwelling in the waters and by sages.
Established in the divine yoga-sleep made of his own maya, Madhusudana contemplates himself, called Vasudeva.
He sleeps for a kalpa; awakened, in Brahma's form he creates again. After two parardhas, O Brahmin, the manifest dissolves into Prakriti.
Place by place the number is multiplied tenfold; the eighteenth place from one is called a "parardha".
Twice a parardha is the natural dissolution, called "prakrita pralaya". Through drought, O Brahmin, and contact with fire, a blaze is kindled.
When the modification beginning with the Great Principle and ending with the particulars has perished, and the dissolution has arrived by Krishna's will,
the waters first swallow the earth's quality, smell and the rest; deprived of its own smell, the earth becomes fit for dissolution.
The waters remain with taste as their essence, taste being their quality; fire drinks it, and when they are gone fire blazes.
Wind swallows fire's quality, form, and the sun; when light has gone, the mighty wind is violently shaken.
Then ether swallows wind's quality, touch; when wind has perished, ether remains soundless, O Brahmin.
The elemental ego (bhutadi) swallows ether's quality, sound; and the Great Principle swallows the ego, which is made of self-conceit.
Earth dissolves into water, water into fire, fire into wind, wind into ether, and ether into the ego.
Prakriti, O Brahmin, swallows the Great Principle: manifest and unmanifest Prakriti; the manifest dissolves into the unmanifest.
The pure imperishable Person is a part of the Supreme Self; Prakriti and Purusha both dissolve in the Supreme Self.
In the Lord of all, where there are no conceptions of name, class and the like, who is to be known as pure being, the Self of knowledge, beyond even the self...
If a soul with sin remaining has enjoyed heaven, then it takes a second body, an enjoying body, of the sinful.
Having enjoyed the sin afterwards, one who had enjoyed heaven, fallen from heaven, is born in the house of the pure and prosperous.
If sin remains with merit, he has enjoyed the sin; when that body is consumed, he takes an auspicious body.
When little of the karma remains, he is freed even from hell; freed from hell, he goes to an animal womb, without doubt.
The soul that has entered the womb remains in the embryo; in the second month it becomes solid, in the third the limbs form.
In the fourth month bones, skin and flesh; in the fifth hair arises; in the sixth consciousness comes; in the seventh the soul feels suffering.
In the body wrapped in the membrane, with joined palms at the head; in the middle a neuter, on the left a female, on the right a male is placed.
It stays in the belly, facing the back; the womb in which it stays, it knows, without doubt.
It knows the whole course of events from the beginning of human birth; and in darkness a man feels great pain.
In the seventh month it partakes of what the mother eats and drinks; in the eighth and ninth month it is greatly agitated.
It suffers pain from the mother's intercourse and from her exertion; sickness comes with her sickness, a moment like a hundred years.
Tormented by his deeds, he forms wishes; "Having come out of the womb, O Brahmin, I shall practise the knowledge of liberation."
Overcome by the winds of birth, he comes out through the womb-passage, pained for a month by the touch of hands.
From ether come the body's hollow channels and ears, and emptiness; breath in and out, the movement of wind, and the sense of touch.
Fire gives form, sight, warmth, digestion, bile; intelligence, colour, strength, lustre, brilliance and valour in the body.
From water arise sweat and the sense of taste; moisture, fat, serum, buttermilk-like fluid, semen, urine, phlegm and the like.
From earth: the nose, hair, nails, heaviness and steadiness. From the mother come the soft parts: skin, flesh, and heart.
Navel, marrow, faeces, fat, fluids and the stomach-cavities; from the father come veins, sinews, and semen; from the self are...
Desire, anger, fear, joy, the nature of dharma and adharma, shape, voice and colour, and the organ of generation and the like.
(Text corrupted in the source; only a note on variant readings of the breathing and touch lines survives.)
The tamasic are ignorance, negligence, laziness, thirst and hunger, delusion, envy, defect, grief, fatigue and fear.
Desire, anger, valour, wish to sacrifice, much talk, egoism and contempt of others are rajasic, O great sage.
Desire for dharma, longing for liberation, supreme devotion to Keshava, courtesy and resolve: these one should declare sattvic.
